definition.name: Combined RCBO
definition.description: This breaker protects one circuit. It can trip on too much current or when some current returns by another path.

terminals.purpose: Incoming L terminal. Follow it to LOUT on the other side of the same pole.

terminals.label: N
terminals.purpose: Incoming neutral terminal. Follow it to NOUT on the other side of the same pole.
Outgoing L terminal. Follow it to LIN on the other side of the same pole.

terminals.label: N
terminals.purpose: Outgoing neutral terminal. Follow it to NIN on the other side of the same pole.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The case holds the working parts in place and keeps them apart.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: Lift the cover on the bench to see the connections underneath.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: A clamp holds the bare end of a wire against the metal terminal.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: These keep the fitting in place. Look for the screws or clips that hold it.

parts.name: Operating mechanism
parts.purpose: This part moves the contacts when you use the control.

parts.name: Contacts
parts.purpose: These metal faces touch to carry current. Moving them apart opens the switch.

parts.name: Current-sensing ring
parts.purpose: Line and neutral pass through this ring. If some current returns by another route, the device senses the difference and can trip.

parts.name: Thermal protection
parts.purpose: A sustained overload heats this part until the protection trips. Trip times in the lab are approximate.

parts.name: Magnetic release
parts.purpose: A large fault current makes this release open the breaker quickly.

parts.name: Test button · T
parts.purpose: With the device on and supplied, press T. A small test current trips it.
